question: How was the dataset annotated?

answer.free_form_answer: intents are annotated manually with guidance from queries collected using a scoping crowdsourcing task
evidence: We defined the intents with guidance from queries collected using a scoping crowdsourcing task, which prompted crowd workers to provide questions and commands related to topic domains in the manner they would interact with an artificially intelligent assistant. We manually grouped data generated by scoping tasks into intents. To collect additional data for each intent, we used the rephrase and scenario crowdsourcing tasks proposed by BIBREF2. For each intent, there are 100 training queries, which is representative of what a team with a limited budget could gather while developing a task-driven dialog system. Along with the 100 training queries, there are 20 validation and 30 testing queries per intent.

answer_short: All tokens were down-cased, end-of-sentence punctuation was removed, duplicate queries were removed and replaced, and queries from a given crowd worker were placed in a single split to reduce bias.
answer_rationale: The annotation process involved preprocessing steps such as token down-casing, removal of end-of-sentence punctuation, and removal of duplicate queries. Additionally, to reduce bias, queries from the same crowd worker were grouped into a single split (train, validation, or test).

question: What is the size of this dataset?

evidence: This paper fills this gap by analyzing intent classification performance with a focus on out-of-scope handling. To do so, we constructed a new dataset with 23,700 queries that are short and unstructured, in the same style made by real users of task-oriented systems. The queries cover 150 intents, plus out-of-scope queries that do not fall within any of the 150 in-scope intents.

question: Where does the data come from?

evidence: We introduce a new crowdsourced dataset of 23,700 queries, including 22,500 in-scope queries covering 150 intents, which can be grouped into 10 general domains. The dataset also includes 1,200 out-of-scope queries. Table TABREF2 shows examples of the data.

answer.free_form_answer:
For ins scope data collection:crowd workers which provide questions and commands related to topic domains and additional data the rephrase and scenario crowdsourcing tasks proposed by BIBREF2 is used. 
For out of scope data collection:  from workers mistakes-queries written for one of the 150 intents that did not actually match any of the intents and using scoping and scenario tasks with prompts based on topic areas found on Quora, Wikipedia, and elsewhere.
evidence: We defined the intents with guidance from queries collected using a scoping crowdsourcing task, which prompted crowd workers to provide questions and commands related to topic domains in the manner they would interact with an artificially intelligent assistant. We manually grouped data generated by scoping tasks into intents. To collect additional data for each intent, we used the rephrase and scenario crowdsourcing tasks proposed by BIBREF2. For each intent, there are 100 training queries, which is representative of what a team with a limited budget could gather while developing a task-driven dialog system. Along with the 100 training queries, there are 20 validation and 30 testing queries per intent.

Out-of-scope queries were collected in two ways. First, using worker mistakes: queries written for one of the 150 intents that did not actually match any of the intents. Second, using scoping and scenario tasks with prompts based on topic areas found on Quora, Wikipedia, and elsewhere. To help ensure the richness of this additional out-of-scope data, each of these task prompts contributed to at most four queries. Since we use the same crowdsourcing method for collecting out-of-scope data, these queries are similar in style to their in-scope counterparts.

title: An Evaluation Dataset for Intent Classification and Out-of-Scope Prediction
answer_short: From scoping crowdsourcing tasks, rephrase and scenario tasks, and worker mistakes, with data sourced from Quora, Wikipedia, and elsewhere.
answer_rationale: The in-scope data was collected via scoping crowdsourcing tasks and supplemented with rephrase and scenario tasks (Text 5). Out-of-scope data was gathered from worker mistakes and scoping/scenario tasks using prompts from Quora, Wikipedia, and other sources (Text 8).
